task.description:
WF-02, step 1b (THIRD and last gate pass: a FAIL stops the run and goes to the owner) — check the design docs/design/REQ-104-e2e-chrome-kit.md after the rework 01e (handoffs/E2E104-20261103-01/step-01e-code-designer.json) by the section "Step 1b" of docs/workflows/WF-02-development.md and by your own second-pass findings F11-F16 in handoffs/E2E104-20261103-01/step-01d-code-design-validator.json. Read the design itself.
Check in particular: (1) F11 is really closed: REPEAT yourself, on a fresh clone of the tag outside the project, that `npm run traces` fails on a captured TAP text with the machine path and passes after the path removal described in section 11.3; that E2K-34 (with hasHomePath/hasTempPath from tools/src/traces/rules.js) would catch the committed fixtures; the criterion-11 grep of REQ-104 gives 0 on the described fixtures and kit text. (2) F12-F16 are closed in the design (section 4.4, 6, 7 rows 12/17/18, E2K-18/37/38/39, M59, section 18 with REQ-040, F16 comment ban E2K-25/50 and M72). (3) The two additions beyond the list (a SPEC_FAILED row for a spec process that cannot start, and the option hookLimitMs) are accepted by ORCH if they are needed to make F13/F14 testable; judge whether they are sensible, not as work beyond the criteria. (4) Nothing new broke: replacement table (six tests), criterion → test table (53 tests: 40 E2K, 13 SMK; criteria 1-13), bar section, no implementation code, no contradiction with decisions 0107/0108 (О9 now also names REQ-040: whether DOC-UPDATER or a micro-amendment corrects it is decided by ORCH at step 10 and is not a reason to FAIL). (5) Apply at least 10 mutants again, at least 5 from M62-M72, plus several of your own around the new signal-hook rules. If you find a missing mutant for "tap text committed with a machine path" say whether it is needed (a remark, not a FAIL, unless a criterion is left unprotected).
Answers of ORCH in decisions/0108 are binding; О7b and REQ-033/REQ-014 are for the owner. A FAIL only for blocking items (a criterion unprotected, a contradiction, an unbuildable or unsafe design); Low items are remarks and go to the developers.
MAC LOAD: one agent at a time; at most one full `npm test`; kill every Chrome you start by process id; remove only temp folders you created; never rm inside the project.
Result: PASS or FAIL with a list (section, item, what is wrong).
acceptance_criteria: Each item of WF-02 step 1b has a stated result

After the removal of `file://<abs>/` and `<abs>/` (section 11.3 step 2) the lines read `location: 'test/fixtures/e2e/specs/fail.e2e.js:3:1'` and `(test/fixtures/e2e/specs/fail.e2e.js:4:9)`, `traces: файлов проверено 2382, следов 0`, exit 0, `npm run -s traces | grep -c -E 'tools/test/e2e|tools/test/fixtures/e2e'` -> 0, prettier --check accepts the folder. Criterion-11 greps on the described fixtures: secret grep exit 1 (no line), skip-word grep exit 1, sandbox-flag grep exit 1; a simulated comment `never pass --no-sandbox` in a kit file turns the 10(d) grep to exit 0 (M72 killed). summary.additions_beyond_the_list: Both ACCEPTED as sensible and needed: the SPEC_FAILED row for a spec process that cannot start (E2K-37) defines the fake child contract that F13(a) needs; the option hookLimitMs of installHandlers (read by the first call only) lets E2K-39 run with a 1 s limit instead of waiting 10 s (otherwise F14's cap and second-signal promises have no affordable test). summary.missing_mutant_machine_path: A numbered mutant 'tap text committed with a machine path' is NOT needed: the oracle exists twice (E2K-34 with hasHomePath/hasTempPath/file:/absolute-path checks turns red on the raw text; the traces step of check turns red on a home-style path) and criterion 11 is protected by the command of RELEASE-VALIDATOR. Blind spot noted only for information: a Windows path with backslashes (`C:\Users\...`) is not seen by hasHomePath (it needs a slash); E2K-34's own drive-letter pattern covers it.
summary.verdict_reason: All items of the applicable passes are met; F11-F16 are closed by my own runs; no criterion is unprotected, no contradiction, the design is buildable. Remarks N1-N6 are Low and go to the developers.

findings.place: section 10, row of criterion 11 (the E2K-50 cell) against section 11.1 row E2K-50
findings.what: Section 10 says E2K-50 also checks 'no `://` outside the `http://127.0.0.1` forms'. The E2K-50 row of 11.1 has no such rule, the requirement criterion 11 has none, and the design's own required text would break it: E2K-20/E2K-21 (`http://example.com/`, `https://127.0.0.1:1/`, `file:///etc/hosts`), SMK-13 (`http://example.com/`, `http://192.0.2.1/`), the `ws://127.0.0.1` pattern of browser.js and fake-chrome.js are all in files E2K-50 scans.
findings.needed: Strike the clause from section 10, or say that 11.1 governs; TEST-DESIGNER implements E2K-50 as the 11.1 row and does not add a `://` rule.

findings.place: section 10, intro sentence 'Every test appears in this table'
findings.what: SMK-09, SMK-10, SMK-11, SMK-12 are not in the table of section 10 (each has its criterion in the column of 11.2: 3, 3, 3, 5).
findings.needed: Add them to the rows of criteria 3 and 5, or soften the sentence; no criterion is unprotected.

findings.what: 'All hooks are called at once and awaited together with one limit' has no test: a mutant that runs the hooks one after another (my X2, each hook awaited in turn, the total limit kept) survives all five cases of E2K-39, because no case has two hooks that finish within the limit. Only the runner registers a hook today, so the effect is nil now.
findings.needed: Either a case with two hooks of about 600 ms each and a 1000 ms limit (both markers expected), or drop 'at once' from 4.4.

findings.place: section 4.4 cleanupAllSync, section 7 row 18 ('no group is signalled twice')
findings.what: cleanupAllSync is called in step 4 of the signal handler and again by the exit handler, and it is not said that it clears the registry; a registered group (the preflight browser) is then sent SIGKILL twice (a gone pid may be reused). The sentence of row 18 is true only for the stopped spec group.
findings.needed: One sentence: cleanupAllSync unregisters what it killed (or the exit handler skips it after the signal path).

findings.place: section 11.1 E2K-34 ('the text of failing holds the line `location: 'test/fixtures/e2e/specs/fail.e2e.js:3:1'` shape')
findings.what: The word 'shape' leaves open whether the exact line:column 3:1 is pinned. Pinned, it ties fail.e2e.js to a fixed layout (import on line 1, the test call on line 3) and to the formatter; unpinned, the assertion is a pattern.
findings.needed: Say which: an exact string (and then the layout of fail.e2e.js is fixed in 11.3) or a pattern `location: 'test/fixtures/e2e/specs/fail.e2e.js:<n>:<n>'`.

findings.place: section 11.1 E2K-22, E2K-23 and the README texts
findings.what: `npm run traces` flags a literal temporary-root or home-folder path in any file (the rule of line-level home paths and, for handoffs, temporary roots); the tests that need a path 'outside the temporary root' must not write one as a literal that looks like a system temporary or home folder. Not stated for the tester.
findings.needed: A half sentence in E2K-22: the outside path is built at run time or is a non-temporary root such as a system folder, not a literal temporary or home path.
